notes.1a: This was very well done with most candidates accurately finding the determinant as 6k−12and setting it to be non-zero. The small number of candidates who instead solved the system of equations in terms of k were less successful.
notes.1b: The strongest candidates gave a full geometric description, stating that the two parallel planes are not identical.
notes.2a: The majority of candidates found the first derivative correctly using implicit differentiation.
notes.2b: The attempts to find the second derivative varied in length, with stronger candidates showing the required level of algebraic fluency when differentiating expressions such as yy' with respect to x and maintaining accuracy when substituting into their expression.
notes.3a: Most candidates accurately recalled the formula for surface area with correct limits. Stronger candidates fully simplified 1+y'2 before substituting into the formula, which caused fewer errors and enabled a clear path to the answer.
notes.3b: The majority of candidates used the expansion of ex correctly. Deriving the Maclaurin’s series by differentiating ex + 1 e −x twice was also a successful approach.
notes.4: Most candidates used the correct method to find the integrating factor, but errors with constants were common and, after multiplying both sides of the equation by their integrating factor, most candidates were able to attempt to integrate the RHS. Stronger candidates maintained accuracy throughout, particularly when substituting in the initial conditions. Most candidates remembered to add an arbitrary constant after integrating the right-hand side, substituted the initial conditions and made x the subject.
notes.5a: Almost all candidates wrote down the four fourth roots of unity, often in exponential or trigonometric form.
notes.5b: After expanding cosθ+isinθ using the binomial expansion, most candidates grouped together terms contributing to the real part before applying the identity cos2θ+sin2θ=1 to fully justify the given result. Alternatively, a few candidates worked from the right-hand side to the left-hand side, applying 2cosθ=z+z −1, and were usually successful too.
notes.5c: Almost all candidates factorised correctly, linking with the previous part of the question. Stronger candidates then solved cos4θ=± 3 , remembering to consider both signs, leading to exactly eight distinct real roots.
notes.6: Stronger candidates showed consideration of the sum of the areas of the rectangles to justify the left-hand side of the inequality. When dealing with the right-hand side, the most common approach was to complete the square and use the logarithmic form of the inverse of cosh to justify the given answer. A small number of candidates worked directly with the natural logarithm via inspection, and were usually successful too.
notes.7a: While it was common to see Ae=λe written, only the strongest candidates gave a correct algebraic argument by multiplying both sides of the equation by A on the left-hand side.
notes.7b: This part was done well with most candidates finding the cross product of two rows of A+I, rather than solving simultaneous equations.
notes.7c: This part of the question was also done well with the majority of candidates finding the correct eigenvalues.
notes.7d: Most candidates took reciprocals of their eigenvalues and matched them correctly to their eigenvectors, but a few candidates accepted zero eigenvectors without checking for errors in their working.
notes.7e: Stronger candidates were able to maintain accuracy when manipulating the characteristic equation, by replacing λ with Aand by multiplying both sides of their equation by A −1.
notes.8a: This part was done well with candidates finding the first two derivatives ofyor, alternatively, u with respect to x and substituting to justify the given equation. Stronger candidates clearly worked from the given y−x equation to the given u−x equation, applying cosh2u−sinh2u =1.
notes.8b: Almost all candidates knew how to approach this question and completed it to a high standard. There was some inaccuracy when solving linear equations to find the constants and some problems with notation. A few candidates gave expressions instead of equations as their answer. More successful approaches involved substituting y =coshu and making u the subject.
notes.key_messages:
• Candidates should show all the steps in their solutions, particularly when proving a given result.
• Candidates should read questions carefully so that they answer all aspects in adequate depth,
particularly when approximating the area under a curve using rectangles.
• Candidates should make use of results derived or given in earlier parts of a question as appropriate.
notes.general_comments:
The majority of candidates demonstrated very good knowledge across the whole syllabus. They showed
their working clearly and were accurate in their handling of algebra and calculus. They also showed
understanding of linear algebra. Sometimes candidates reached conclusions without justification, particularly
where answers were given within the question. There were many responses of a high standard.
